title: Failforward capacity-slope router with latency-tiered fallthrough
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Summary:
We need a routing policy that prioritizes both latency SLOs and remaining regional capacity while avoiding hard failovers that cause large tail-latency spikes. The proposed 'failforward capacity-slope router' uses: (1) latency-tiered preference buckets, (2) capacity slope scoring (capacity remaining normalized by recent token consumption rate), and (3) a graded fallthrough that can 'fail forward' to cheaper/quantized model variants or truncated responses before failing across regions.

Motivation & context:
- Current geo pin and latency-based routing cause binary switchovers when a region crosses a threshold, producing sharp traffic shifts and increased error rates in destination regions.
- We observe cascading latencies when the primary region hits autoscaler cold starts or transient GPU queuing; customers see large 95/99p latency regressions even when global capacity exists.
- Goals: keep 99p latency within SLO where reasonable, avoid sudden traffic rebalances, reduce inter-region egress spikes, and provide predictable customer experience under constrained capacity.

Design overview:
- Input signals: per-region p50/p95/p99 latency histograms (last 5m), rolling token consumption rate (tokens/s per region), available capacity units (fractional GPU slots), model variant inventory (fp16, int8, quantized-4), and region health tags.
- Scoring: compute a composite score = latency_penalty * w1 + capacity_slope_penalty * w2 + locality_bonus * w3.
  - latency_penalty: sigmoid(p99 - target99) scaled to 0..1.
  - capacity_slope_penalty: normalized negative slope of available capacity over last 60s (rising slope good -> low penalty).
  - locality_bonus: small constant favoring origin-proximal regions (reduces jitter for sticky users).
- Failforward tiers: when preferred region score degrades beyond tier thresholds, we transition traffic in stages:
  1) Local degrade: enable prefix caching and increase batching for matching tokens.
  2) Model degrade: route a configurable percentage to a compatible quantized model variant in the same region.
  3) Response degrade: for permissive routes, enable token-limited responses (truncate or summarization heuristic) with explicit response headers.
  4) Cross-region failover only after other tiers and a graded cooldown window.

Circuit breaker integration:
- Implement a per-region CB with three states (Closed, Throttled, Open).
  - Transition to Throttled when p99 > 2x SLO or error rate spike > 5% in 60s. Throttled will cap new concurrent requests to a soft quota and apply failforward model degrade.
  - Open when persistent error/latency persists for 3 windows; Open triggers aggressive shedding and mandatory cross-region fallback.
- Exponential backoff retries for Open->Closed transitions and a hysteresis window to avoid flip-flopping.

Load-shedding policy:
- Token-budgeted shedding: maintain a global budget per region that subtracts weighted tokens for each request type. When budget < low_watermark, start shedding lowest-priority routes first (experimental, rerank, non-critical ingestion).
- Priority vector: interactive-chat > sync-generation > embedding > batch-transform. Shedding respects route-level priority and customer SLA tiers.

Observability & SLOs:
- New metrics: failforward_stage (none/local/model/response/cross-region), capacity_slope, composite_score, circuit_breaker_state, shed_count_by_route, model_variant_routing_pct.
- Dashboards: per-region failforward timeline overlayed with p99, available_capacity, and egress_volume.
- Alerts: automated pager when cross-region failover rate > 3% of global traffic for 10min or when shed_rate for P0 customers > 0.5% in 5m.

API/config surface:
- Feature-flag controlled: routing.failforward.enabled (default false in prod until canary passes).
- Per-customer overrides: allow customers to opt-out of model/response degrade with route-level metadata.
- Admin UI: slider for capacity_slope weight and failforward cooldown.

Rollout plan:
1) Unit + integration tests for scoring and CB logic.
2) Canary in dedicated region with low traffic (feature flag + 1% traffic).
3) Expand to 10% and monitor failforward metrics and downstream latency.
4) 50% with gradual parameter tuning.
5) Full launch and deprecation of older binary threshold routing.

Trade-offs considered:
- Complexity vs predictability: scoring adds more parameters but significantly smooths traffic transitions compared to hard thresholds.
- Customer control vs platform safety: allowing opt-outs for model degrade preserves fidelity for some customers but increases cost and risk during emergencies; default is conservative degrade.
- Cross-region egress: graded fallback reduces sudden egress bursts but introduces slightly longer period of degraded responses.

Open questions / risks:
- Weight calibration (w1..w3): need offline simulation harness using 30d production traces.
- How to ensure failforward headers are surfaced to SDKs and not dropped by intermediate proxies.
- Impact on billing semantics when model degrade or truncated responses are applied.

References & artifacts:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RR/Failforward+Capacity-Slope+Router (internal draft)
- Simulation harness PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/traffic-sim/pull/142 (WIP)
- Prototype implementation: https://github.com/redwood-inference/routebox/compare/failforward-prototype (branch)
- Dashboard mock: https://dashboards.redwood.ai/d/ff-router/proto (read-only)

Next steps (short term):
- Hook up production latency histograms into the scoring library (ENG infra task).
- Build a small offline simulator to tune weights and thresholds (assigned: Marcus Lee).
- Create an e2e test that asserts no more than 10% traffic shift in 60s during simulated region capacity drops.
